title: Committee of Supply – Head R (Ministry of Law)
what_it_is: Committee of Supply – Head R (Ministry of Law)

sections.label: iLab free legal chatbox
sections.summary: iLab is a free legal chatbox giving legal information on nine modules, and in 2021 it registered 47,500 queries in 3,408 sessions.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: One major initiative, which has received good reviews from members of public, is the iLab, which is a free legal chatbox that provides legal information on nine modules which include COVID-19 legal issues, monetary claims in addition to the usual family law issues.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: In 2021 alone, iLab registered 47,500 queries in 3,408 sessions.

sections.label: Raising PCHI means limit
sections.summary: The speaker proposes raising the current Per Capita Gross Monthly Household Income means limit of $950, last adjusted in October 2019.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: Next, to further strengthen access to justice for persons of limited means, I wish to propose that the current means limit of the Per Capita Gross Monthly Household Income (PCHI) of $950, which was last adjusted in October 2019, be raised.

sections.label: Reviewing PCHI and means test waiver
sections.summary: The speaker suggests studying a PCHI review, publicising the Means Test Panel's waiver discretion, and notes seven applications since 2019, five approved.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: Given that there is a capacity to take on more cases, I suggest that a study be done to review the PCHI and study the feasibility of revising it upwards.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: I also suggest that the Ministry make it better known that there is a discretion given to the Means Test Panel to waive the means test requirements when it is found to be "just and proper" to do so.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: I learned from MinLaw's recent response to my Parliamentary Question that since 2019, when the amendments to the Legal Aid and Advice Act to provide for flexibility in providing legal aid was introduced, the Means Test Panel only received seven applications, of which five were approved.

sections.label: Judgment debtors and legal efficiencies
sections.summary: Provisions exist for judgment debtors who withhold honest answers or fraudulently remove assets, and the speaker spoke on capturing efficiencies from chatbots and new technologies.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: In any event, there exists provisions to deal with judgment debtors who are not forthcoming with honest answers or fraudulently remove their assets to frustrate judgment creditors.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: Mr Chairman, Sir, I have spoken on the need to capture all possible efficiencies, including from chatbots and new technologies, to ensure that the provision of justice remains a lean and streamlined process.

sections.label: Reviewing means test and laws
sections.summary: The speaker asks for a means test review and smaller reviews to keep laws updated and coherent, efficient, accessible and trusted.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: In this, I ask for us to review the means test.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: Last, I ask for a few smaller reviews to ensure that our laws are updated and made coherent with developments across the entire body of law.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: Together, they ensure that our legal system remains efficient, accessible and coherent, all of which will go a long way towards maintaining and building up that trust that Singaporeans have in our laws.

sections.label: Study on enforcing civil judgments
sections.summary: The speaker notes the Government's plan to study streamlining enforcement of civil judgments and asks the Minister for an update and reform plans.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sitoh Yih Pin (Potong Pasir)
sentences.text: It requires investing further time and resources and this could sometimes be to the detriment of the successful party.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sitoh Yih Pin (Potong Pasir)
sentences.text: I was therefore quite pleased when Second Minister for Law Edwin Tong had, at a previous Committee of Supply debate, alluded to the Government’s plan to study measures to streamline and simplify the enforcement of civil judgments and orders.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sitoh Yih Pin (Potong Pasir)
sentences.text: In the premises, I invite the Minister to share an update with this House of the Government’s study and whether there are plans to push ahead with any recommendations to reform the legal process in the area of enforcement.

sections.label: Civil enforcement process review for workers
sections.summary: The passage asks whether MinLaw is reviewing civil enforcement to make it more accessible, economical, expeditious and less painful for workers and the layman.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (Pioneer)
sentences.text: Workers’ lack of knowledge of the workings of our Court system exacerbates this problem.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (Pioneer)
sentences.text: There is thus a need to simplify and expedite the enforcement mechanism to facilitate workers’ recovery of monies.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (Pioneer)
sentences.text: Can I therefore ask if MinLaw is reviewing this entire civil enforcement process to make enforcement more accessible, economical, expeditious and less painful for workers and the layman?

sections.label: Conditional fee arrangements for lawyers
sections.summary: The passage states that conditional fee arrangements could be considered, allowing lawyers outcome-based payments instead of fixed payments.

sentences.speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
sentences.text: The first is that we can consider permitting conditional fee arrangements for these situations as well, meaning that lawyers can have outcome-based payments rather than collecting fixed payments.

sections.label: Spousal disadvantage and maintenance orders
sections.summary: The passage states some feel disadvantaged when the other spouse is better educated and controls finances, and that maintenance orders are sometimes not followed.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng (Jurong)
sentences.text: Some feel disadvantaged, especially if the other spouse is better educated and controls the family's finances.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng (Jurong)
sentences.text: Even where the Court has issued orders in favour of one party, there are cases of maintenance orders not being followed.

sections.label: Earning too much for legal aid
sections.summary: The passage states some do not earn enough to engage a lawyer but earn too much to qualify for legal aid.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng (Jurong)
sentences.text: Some do not earn enough to engage a lawyer, but earn too much to qualify for legal aid.

sections.label: Unclaimed CPF monies and Beneficiary Representative
sections.summary: The passage states 2% of CPF monies were unclaimed in 2018, and the Central Provident Fund Act was amended to take a Beneficiary Representative approach.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim
sentences.text: In 2018, it was reported that 2% of CPF monies were unclaimed, amounting to $132 million.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim
sentences.text: Last year, the Central Provident Fund Act was amended to take a "Beneficiary Representative" (BR) approach to simplify the payment of deceased CPF members’ un-nominated CPF monies.

sections.label: Addressing lawyers leaving the profession
sections.summary: The passage suggests MinLaw could consider upping the proportion of graduate law students and extending the MOE Tuition Grant to all graduate law students.

sentences.speaker: Mr Raj Joshua Thomas (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: If we accept stress as an immutable part of the profession, we have to then look at other things that can be changed to address the exodus of junior and middle category lawyers from the profession.

sentences.speaker: Mr Raj Joshua Thomas (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: First, MinLaw could consider upping the proportion of law students in our Universities who are graduate students.

sentences.speaker: Mr Raj Joshua Thomas (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: The MOE Tuition Grant should also be extended to all graduate law students, regardless of whether they had utilised the grant for their earlier degree.

sections.label: Lawyers leaving profession
sections.summary: A record 538 lawyers left the profession in 2021, most of them junior.

sentences.speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: A record number of 538 lawyers left the profession in 2021, most of whom were in the junior category.

sections.label: Retaining young legal talent
sections.summary: The question asks what plans the Government has to work with the legal sector to attract, manage and retain young legal talent sustainably.

sentences.speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: What plans does the Government have to work with the legal sector to attract, manage and retain young legal talent sustainably in the long run?

sections.label: Pandemic shifts legal working
sections.summary: The pandemic shifted the legal profession to a new normal of working from home and attending hearings via Zoom.

sentences.speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza
sentences.text: The pandemic has shifted the legal profession to a new normal of working from home and attending hearings via Zoom.

sections.label: Technology in law practice
sections.summary: Technology is increasingly important in law practice, but many law practices struggle with digitalisation, archive conversion and funding computer and software upgrades.

sentences.speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza
sentences.text: Technology is becoming an increasingly important element in the practice and business of law, with Zoom hearings, Artificial Intelligence (AI) being utilised to perform due diligence and research and data analytics providing prediction, thereby, saving time.

sentences.speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza
sentences.text: However, many law practices continue to struggle with the digitalisation journey, such as converting archive files and paperwork to digital records and having the necessary funds to upgrade computers and software to keep up to date.

sections.label: Singapore dispute resolution centre
sections.summary: Singapore has steadily built a reputation as an international dispute resolution centre over the past few decades.

sentences.speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza
sentences.text: Singapore has steadily built a reputation as an international dispute resolution centre over the past few decades.

sections.label: Intellectual Property in innovation economy
sections.summary: Intellectual Property plays an increasingly important role in an innovation-driven economy, particularly with blockchain, cryptocurrency and NFTs.

sentences.speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza
sentences.text: Intellectual Property, or IP, plays an increasingly important role in an innovation-driven economy, particularly with the rise of blockchain and cryptocurrency, as well as perhaps non-fungible tokens or NFTs.

sections.label: Simpler enforcement of court orders
sections.summary: Changes will simplify enforcement, including new powers against non-compliance, asset tracing, and application to Employment Claims Tribunal orders.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
sentences.text: To address this, we will introduce changes designed to make enforcement simpler and more streamlined – a point also picked up by Mr Sitoh Yih Pin and Mr Patrick Tay.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
sentences.text: SMEs and litigants-in-person, in particular, will benefit from these changes.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
sentences.text: These include introducing new powers to punish and disincentivise non-compliance with Court orders.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
sentences.text: And if a party still fails to comply, the Courts will be given enhanced powers to track and trace assets of the judgment debtor.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
sentences.text: Specifically on Mr Tay's concerns on workers encountering difficulties enforcing Employment Claims Tribunal or ECT orders, the proposals I mentioned are intended to apply to ECT orders as well.

sections.label: Family justice reforms amendments
sections.summary: Work with MSF and the Family Justice Courts will effect recommendations of the Committee to Review and Enhance Reforms in the Family Justice System, with legislative amendments later this year.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
sentences.text: To take these objectives further, we have been working with MSF and the Family Justice Courts (FJC) to effect the recommendations of the Committee to Review and Enhance Reforms in the Family Justice System.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
sentences.text: We are looking at legislative amendments later this year.

sections.label: Review of Debtors Act
sections.summary: The Debtors Act will be reviewed at the appropriate juncture and reforms proposed if necessary.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
sentences.text: We thank Mr Murali Pillai for highlighting this.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
sentences.text: We will review the Debtors Act at the appropriate juncture and, if necessary, propose reforms.

sections.label: Studied community dispute measures
sections.summary: Measures being studied include mandatory mediation in some cases, enhanced CDRT processes, and an appropriate response protocol for disputes.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
sentences.text: Measures that we are studying include: (a)	making mediation mandatory in some cases; (b)	enhancing the Community Disputes Resolution Tribunals' (CDRT) processes to address pain points, including some of the present difficulties involved in the CDRT process; and, finally, (c) having an appropriate response protocol to address disputes quickly and effectively.

sections.label: Beneficiary representation for small claims
sections.summary: An eligible beneficiary can represent all beneficiaries for cases up to $10,000, with implementation targeted for the second quarter of this year.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
sentences.text: So, a fairly big proportion of the unnominated sums will come under this approach.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
sentences.text: We are focusing on implementing this by the second quarter of this year.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
sentences.text: Under this process, an eligible beneficiary can represent all beneficiaries for cases up to $10,000.

sections.label: E-service guided questions and forms
sections.summary: The e-service will use guided questions to help applicants provide information and fill up Court forms.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
sentences.text: Beyond personal particulars, the e-service will also use guided questions to help applicants provide the relevant information – information that allows their applications to be processed more quickly – and use that to help applicants fill up the Court forms, which sometimes present a chokepoint, even at the start of the process itself.

sections.label: Conditional fee agreements for arbitration
sections.summary: CFAs will be permitted as an additional litigation funding option for arbitration, certain SICC proceedings and related Court and mediation proceedings.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
sentences.text: Under this new framework, CFAs will be permitted as an additional litigation funding option for arbitration proceedings, certain proceedings in the Singapore International Commercial Court (SICC) and related Court and mediation proceedings.

sections.label: Damages-based awards not allowed
sections.summary: The decision was not to allow damages-based awards presently, as fees would have no direct correlation to the quantum and value of work done.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
sentences.text: On Mr Vikram Nair's other point, we had considered whether to allow damages-based awards but decided not to do so, at least presently, as such an approach means that fees that one charges will have no direct correlation to the quantum and value of the work done by the lawyer.

sections.label: Singapore arbitration survey rankings
sections.summary: In the 2021 Queen Mary and White & Case survey, Singapore ranked as top arbitration seat globally alongside London, and SIAC was most preferred in Asia Pacific and second worldwide.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
sentences.text: In the 2021 Queen Mary University of London and White & Case International Arbitration Survey, Singapore was ranked as top arbitration seat globally, alongside London, and Singapore International Arbitration Centre (SIAC) was the most preferred arbitral institution in the Asia Pacific and second in the world.

sections.label: Lawyers leaving the profession
sections.summary: In 2021, about 20% more lawyers left the profession compared to the average of the preceding three years.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
sentences.text: In 2021, about 20% more lawyers left the profession, compared to the average of the preceding three years.

sections.label: New entrants exceeded those leaving
sections.summary: The number of new entrants exceeded those who left the profession every year for the past four years, at least since 2018.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
sentences.text: In fact, the number of new entrants exceeded those who left the profession every year for the past four years, at least since 2018, when we kept a data bank of the numbers.

sections.label: Professional training recommendations accepted
sections.summary: MinLaw accepted recommendations including lengthening the Practice Training Period from six months to a year, and will review training and education and explore an industry-wide secondment programme.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
sentences.text: MinLaw earlier accepted the recommendations of the Committee for the Professional Training of Lawyers.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
sentences.text: This includes lengthening the Practice Training Period from six months to a year, to allow trainees to develop a stronger foundation in legal practice before they embark on legal practice.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
sentences.text: We will also review the training and education for law students, lawyers and allied legal professionals, including the need for leadership and management training, a good suggestion by Mr Raj Joshua Thomas.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
sentences.text: We will work with the Law Society to explore an industry-wide secondment programme to enhance our presence in important markets, such as in China, and also in important domains, such as in sustainability, M&A and technology.

sections.label: Legal Technology Transformation Office
sections.summary: The Ministry set up a Legal Technology Transformation Office to support law firms and will launch the Legal Technology Platform.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
sentences.text: Within the Ministry, we have set up a new Legal Technology Transformation Office, specifically to provide dedicated resources to support law firms on this journey.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
sentences.text: We will also be launching the Legal Technology Platform (LTP) shortly.

sections.label: Encouraging law firm adoption
sections.summary: The Ministry will work with Enterprise Singapore, IMDA and Law Society to encourage adoption among small and medium-sized law firms and explore grants for early adopters.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
sentences.text: We will work with Enterprise Singapore, IMDA and Law Society to encourage adoption amongst small and medium-sized law firms.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
sentences.text: We will also be exploring grants for early adopters to defray the subscription cost of the LTP and selected LTP-integrated solutions.

sections.label: Global intangible asset value
sections.summary: In 2021, the global value of intangible assets reached US$74 trillion.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
sentences.text: In 2021, the global value of intangible assets reached US$74 trillion.

sections.label: IPOS SG IP Fast Track
sections.summary: Enterprises can obtain IP protection quickly through the Intellectual Property Office of Singapore's acceleration programme, SG IP Fast Track.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
sentences.text: Enterprises can obtain IP protection quickly through the Intellectual Property Office of Singapore’s (IPOS) acceleration programme, SG IP Fast Track.

sections.label: Internationally-recognised IA/IP valuation
sections.summary: A uniform internationally-recognised platform sets the valuation methodology for IA/IP across jurisdictions, creating opportunities for valuers and supporting Singapore as a business hub.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
sentences.text: This enables us to have a uniform platform, one that is internationally-recognised, on which we can say, if you have an IA or IP, this is the valuation methodology and this is how it will be recognised across different jurisdictions.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
sentences.text: This, in turn, will create more opportunities for IA/IP valuers in Singapore, anchor IA/IP valuation activities and thought leadership here and support Singapore as a trusted business and financial hub.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
sentences.text: IA/IP valuation based on internationally-recognised guidelines is also critical to enabling enterprises to transact and effectively monetise their IA/IP both in Singapore and overseas.

sections.label: Maximising state property value
sections.summary: State properties are to be maximised through good upkeep, enhancements, more productive land uses, and new ideas creating economic and social returns.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
sentences.text: First, to maximise the utilisation of state properties through good upkeep and enhancements, and by putting state land to more productive uses.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
sentences.text: Second, to unlock greater value from our state properties through new and innovative ideas which create greater economic and social returns.

sections.label: Valuation hub and Syariah probate
sections.summary: A speaker urges IPOS to work with IE Singapore, accountants and lawyers to develop a valuation hub, and asks about synergising Muslim law probate with the Family Justice Court.

sentences.speaker: Mr Don Wee (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: Maybe I would urge IPOS to work with IE Singapore, as well as the accountants and the lawyers, to develop Singapore into a regional or worldwide valuation hub.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: Mr Don Wee can be assured that we look at this as a multi-disciplinary cross-cutting approach and, certainly, there will be opportunities for the business community, including the accountants, as Mr Don Wee has put it, to work with us on this.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim
sentences.text: I think there is also the need to synergise with the Muslim law probate process as well because there is a need for Muslim intestate beneficiaries to also extract Syariah inheritance certification from the Syariah Court; and whether there will be also plans to synergise the two systems, so that there will be a seamless transfer of documents and the certificate from the Syariah Court to the Family Justice Court, which may be administering the family justice or the probate and the letter of administration process.

sections.label: Applicants' application process
sections.summary: The passage states that applicants will go through a process to make their application, which can be looked at behind the scenes in the eService.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: And for the applicants to make their application, there will be some process.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: So, we can look at that behind the scenes in the eService that I talked about.

sections.label: Restorative justice when appropriate
sections.summary: The passage states restorative justice will be considered as and when it is appropriate, with the appropriate set of facts, context and cases.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: But it has got to be the appropriate set of facts and context and the appropriate cases.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: So, restorative justice will be considered, as and when it is appropriate.
